subject: POC: Query Bank transfer & eval SLA roadmap
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sam Green <sam.green@peregrine.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC: Query Bank transfer & eval SLA roadmap

Hi Sam — great chat today, thanks for the time. This thread captures the follow-ups and a proposed timeline so we have a single source of truth. I pulled together the items we discussed on the call and a straightforward acceptance path for the POC. Please confirm anything I mis-stated.

Recap of what Peregrine will provide:
- A representative "query bank" (sample of 2k–5k user queries) with basic metadata columns (timestamp, user_id hashed, intent tag, original text) — sample file or export by end of week.
- 1–2 redlines / problem statement examples where current results are unacceptable (for qualitative eval).
- A contact in procurement to receive the MPA draft.

Redwood commitments:
- We will ingest the sample query bank into a private test bucket and map fields for evaluation within 48 hours of receipt.
- Provide an initial eval report (quant + qualitative) within 5 business days of ingest showing latency, recall@k for retrieval scenarios, and a 10-case qualitative review.
- Propose an Eval SLA doc (attached draft) with acceptance thresholds and timelines — review with your team Tuesday.

Proposed milestones & owners:
1) Sample transfer (Peregrine) — Sam — target: 2028-06-16
2) Ingest & schema validation (Redwood Eng) — Ben — target: 2028-06-18
3) Initial evaluation pass (Redwood Solutions) — Marissa — target: 2028-06-23
4) Review & acceptance decision (Peregrine) — Sam + Procurement — target: 2028-06-27

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Automated metric thresholds met: mean token latency < 120ms, retrieval recall@10 >= 0.72 for the provided labeled subset.
- No PII leakage in sampled outputs.
- Qualitative sign-off on 10 prioritized failure cases (3 must be improved).

Attachments in this email: redwood_eval-sla-draft.md (draft SLA and eval rubric).

Next steps for you (Sam):
- Drop the sample query bank to the Drive link or directly attach to reply.
- Confirm procurement contact for contract routing.

If that all looks right I’ll start the ingest plan and loop Ben directly on the calendar invites.

Thanks,
Olga
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132
From: Sam Green <sam.green@peregrine.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@peregrine.ai
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 09:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: Query Bank transfer & eval SLA roadmap

Thanks Olga — good summary and yes, that matches what we spoke about. I attached a small multiplex sample (peregrine_query_bank_sample.csv) — ~1,200 rows, anonymized user_id, and a simple intent label. There are two notes inline in the file about timezones and a nonstandard encoding for a subset of historical logs.

We also attached our draft MPA routing to contracts (mpa-draft-for-peregrine.pdf) — procurement will take a look and loop in their legal review.

A couple clarifications from our side:
- The labeled subset for recall should be 300 rows from the sample. We can flag those in an extra column ("eval_holdout=true").
- For qualitative review, we will supply 12 priority failure cases rather than 10 — happy to let your team pick the top 10 to evaluate.

I’ve included procurement on Cc (contracts@peregrine.ai) — they asked for the MPA and an estimated completion time for the POC so they can map to budget. Do you have a one-sentence summary of the POC scope I can forward internally?

Best,
Sam Green
Sr. Product Manager
Peregrine Analytics
sam.green@peregrine.ai
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: POC: Query Bank transfer & eval SLA roadmap

Marissa/Ben — forwarding Peregrine's sample and procurement note. Key items for our sprint this week: ingest the CSV, validate the eval_holdout flag exists (Sam said they will add it), and run a smoke eval focusing on latency + recall on the 300 holdout rows. Sam expects initial results for procurement to justify the budget timeline.

Ben — can you pick up the ingest and post a short schema mapping to the Drive link (I created a /peregrine-poc folder)? If you hit the timezone/encoding rows flag Sam mentioned, let me know and I’ll coordinate a quick call.

Marissa — after Ben’s ingest, can you run the initial eval checklist (I attached the eval SLA draft earlier) and capture the top 12 failure cases into the shared doc for qualitative review? We’ll aim to surface 3 clear improvements.

I drafted a single-line POC scope for procurement: "Redwood will ingest Peregrine's representative query bank, run a quantitative evaluation (latency, recall) and a qualitative review of prioritized failure cases, and deliver a report within 5 business days of successful ingest." Feel free to shorten.

Thanks — I’ll block a 30-min sync on Thurs for quick triage.
Olga
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sam Green <sam.green@peregrine.ai>, contracts@peregrine.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: RE: POC: Query Bank transfer & eval SLA roadmap — confirmation & next steps

Sam / Procurement — thanks for the file and the MPA draft. Quick confirmation after ingest: we validated the schema, the eval_holdout column is present and flagged on 300 rows, and we ran a smoke pass. Attached are the ingest notes and the initial smoke-summary (see Drive link).

Immediate outcomes: 
- Ingest completed: 2028-06-13 09:18 PDT (Ben)
- Smoke eval delivered: 2028-06-14 09:45 PDT (Marissa)
- Preliminary metrics: mean token latency = 104ms, retrieval recall@10 = 0.69 (on the labeled holdout) — see attached summary for per-intent breakdown.

Action items (ownership & ETA):
- Detailed eval report + qualitative 12-case file (Marissa) — due 2028-06-18
- Quick triage session to go over failure cases (All) — 2028-06-19 10:00 PDT (calendar invite sent)
- Procurement review: legal to come back with comments on MPA (Procurement) — target 2028-06-22

Note on acceptance: recall@10 is below the threshold we proposed (0.72). The qualitative review will prioritize which failure types are most actionable. If we can show targeted improvements on at least 3 of the 12 priority cases and bump recall to >=0.72 on a second eval pass, we can consider moving forward to a limited production pilot.

Attachments referenced: peregrine_query_bank_sample.csv (original), redwood_eval-sla-draft.md (draft rubric), ingest-notes-olga-20280613.md (internal), mpa-draft-for-peregrine.pdf (sent to procurement).

Thanks — looking forward to the triage tomorrow.
Olga
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
